title: Immaculate Constellation as quarantine of communications

tellings.quote: and you need you need some sort of immaculate constellation to quarantine some of the comms both from a kind of you know physical perspective if there are crashed UFOs

plain: Michels suggests that a secret programme called Immaculate Constellation would be needed to "quarantine" communications, and physical material too if there are crashed UFOs. He says this himself on the show. The name comes from an unsigned report that the writer Michael Shellenberger gave to Congress and that Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of a House Oversight hearing on 13 November 2024 as a Pentagon document. The report calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department. A former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown later said he wrote it, and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a programme by that name. The report says the programme "enforces compartmentalization" by "detecting, quarantining, and transferring" incidents caught on imagery "before they are circulated within the Military Intelligence Enterprise", which it says partly explains why cleared military and intelligence staff "are unaware of UAP activities" (UAP is the government's newer word for UFOs). What it says is quarantined is imagery. Whether that also covers communications or crashed craft, as Michels takes it, the report does not say.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report says the program "enforces compartmentalization by detecting, quarantining, and transferring UAP and RV imagery collection incidents before they are circulated within the Military Intelligence Enterprise", "partially explaining why many otherwise cleared members of the military and IC are unaware of UAP activities". What it quarantines is imagery collection incidents; Jesse Michels' quarantine of communications, and of crashed craft, is his widening of that.
